name: No-Gi Competition Approach
description: A rules-comparison study guide for no-gi competitors changing events or experience divisions.
summary: Compare IBJJF and ADCC scoring and division restrictions before choosing a no-gi match plan.
overview: No-gi describes attire, not a single ruleset. ADCC uses scoring phases and negative points, while IBJJF has its own scoring and penalty structure. Even within ADCC, the beginner/intermediate supplement changes permitted techniques and timing. Choose your division before importing tactics from a championship match.

start_here.title: Check an opening choice in the right match phase
start_here.task: Select an actual division and identify the applicable rule document. Compare its opening phase with its scoring phase: when do positive and negative points begin, and what does it say about voluntarily going to the ground? Then look up one submission you already study in that division’s restrictions. Record the relevant passages beside your planned opening rather than assuming a professional match supplies permission.

flashcards.question: Is a qualifying mount worth the same points in IBJJF and the cited ADCC championship rules?
flashcards.answer: No. IBJJF awards four; the ADCC championship rules award two when points apply and the position meets the required conditions.

flashcards.question: Does the ADCC professional championship list establish permitted submissions for every beginner or Masters division?
flashcards.answer: No. The official division supplement lists different restrictions and assigns Masters categories to specified rule groups.
